messages.author: 3c19c581c120208c
messages.subject: RE: reproducibility filter
parts:
Hi everyone,

So I run my DArT sequence data through a series of filters in dartR: 1st is for clones (gl.filter.cloneid) and 2nd through the reproducibility filter (gl.filter.reproducibility). 

# filter for clones
Hsc.gl0 <- gl.filter.cloneid(Hsc.gl)
nLoc(Hsc.gl0)                ### 74605 loci retained
nInd(Hsc.gl0)                ### 178 inds retained
nPop(Hsc.gl0)                ### 7 pops retained

# filter by reproducibility/measure of quality per loci
Hsc.gl1 <- gl.filter.reproducibility(Hsc.gl0, threshold = 0.95, verbose = 2)
nLoc(Hsc.gl1)                ### 72491 loci retained
nInd(Hsc.gl1)                ### 178 inds retained
nPop(Hsc.gl1)                ### 7 pops retained

However, when I repeat the process, I get a different number of retained loci after filtering for reproducibility.

# filter for clones
Hsc.gl0 <- gl.filter.cloneid(Hsc.gl)
nLoc(Hsc.gl0)                ### 74605 loci retained
nInd(Hsc.gl0)                ### 178 inds retained
nPop(Hsc.gl0)                ### 7 pops retained

# filter by reproducibility/measure of quality per loci
Hsc.gl1 <- gl.filter.reproducibility(Hsc.gl0, threshold = 0.95, verbose = 2)
nLoc(Hsc.gl1)                ### 72498 loci retained
nInd(Hsc.gl1)                ### 178 inds retained
nPop(Hsc.gl1)                ### 7 pops retained

The difference, in my experience, ranges from a few loci like this example to sometimes hundreds - and I'm just wondering if this is normal? Thank you.

Deo

messages.author: b3d929c6746ca81a
messages.subject: RE: [dartR] RE: reproducibility filter
parts:
Hi Deo,

 

The filter cloneid has a “random” element. If there are non unique ids (meaning more than one snp within a normally 69 sequence, it choose a random one of those to be included. Therefore it will happen that the randomly chosen ones have a different reproducibility value.

 

And yes I agree a better method would be to select based on some quality measure instead of random.

 

Overall it might not be important in most cases, as most often the difference is small.

We aim to implement a better than random selection in an upcoming version.

 

Cheers, Bernd

messages.author: 9e12eec50c435b60
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] RE: reproducibility filter
parts:
I think gl.filter.cloneid is deprecated. You should use gl.filter.secondaries which gives you the option to select a sequence tag at random or based on reproducibility and AvgPIC in that order.

Let me know if that suits your purposes, or if we should flag an issue in regards to that function.

Note that gl.filter.secondaries with the random option will give slightly different results each time it is run, and hence downstream filtering will give slightly different results.

A
